newsitem.title: UK: UK minister warns on pensions mis-selling reviews.
newsitem.headline: UK minister warns on pensions mis-selling reviews.

text.p: British pension companies made further progress during July in clearing up pensions mis-selling but figures are still disappointing, economic secretary Helen Liddell said on Sunday.

"The July figures show most firms have improved on their June performance...I am encouraged by anecdotal evidence of progress on the ground but, overall, the figures are still disappointing," she said in a statement.
The Treasury promised in June to issue monthly updates on the cases handled by the 24 firms with most cases to review.
Liddell said she would consider what further action was called for "once I have seen some further figures to measure progress".
She said the next few months would be crucial, adding that "all firms must seize the opportunity to demonstrate their commitment and really get a move on in redressing victims".
Many people were wrongly advised to move out of company pension schemes into personal pensions in the late 1980s and early 1990s.

The Financial Times newspaper, in its Monday edition, said the figures showed that only Barclays had completed more than half its 16,722 cases and added that the monthly figures showed that of the total 570,000 cases outstanding, 46,000 had now received redress, amounting to barely eight percent. -- London Newsroom +44171 542 7717
